Chernivtsi New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernivetska oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Chernivtsi's new Jewish cemetery, founded by the municipality in 1866 and designed as a garden complex by the engineer Rally and designer Gaimbe, holds the graves of roughly 50,000 people, including the city's first Jewish mayor, Edward Reiss; the poet Eliezer Steinbarg; Chief Rabbi Benno Straucher; and numerous other named politicians, philanthropists, and physicians who shaped Chernivtsi's civic life. Its elaborate mausoleums and sarcophagi were crafted by named sculptors including B. Reder and the Moskalyuki brothers. The city's most celebrated native son, Abraham Goldfaden (1840–1908), is widely credited as the father of modern Yiddish theater. During Romanian occupation from July 1941, a ghetto imprisoned some 50,000 Jews, crowding 5 to 8 families into each flat, before roughly 30,000 were deported to Transnistria that autumn; a Jewish underground organization, led by M. Batero, Y. Deisch, and L. Reiter, operated throughout the occupation. Since 1995, the cemetery has formed part of the official 'Cemetery on Zelena Street' historical and cultural reserve.
